title: Existence and uniqueness of the finite-type logarithmic image ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $M$ a fine log structure and $\mathcal I\subset M$ a nonempty fine coherent log ideal [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-trf-fine-log-etale-descent-datum]. There is ideal sheaf data $K$ on $X$ whose module is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] and which algebraizes the structural image of $\mathcal I$: on every small-etale object $w:W\to X$, the canonical tensor inclusion $w^*K\to\mathcal O_W$ is monic and its top-section range consists precisely of functions whose every geometric germ belongs to the ideal generated by $\alpha(\mathcal I)$ [def-trf-log-ideal-algebraization-data]. Every ideal sheaf datum $L$ with this same algebraization property equals $K$. This asserts existence, finite type and uniqueness; no chart formula, overlap transitions or strict base-change conclusion is included.

source.place: VIII 3.3.7, printed p. 107, and 3.4.2, printed p. 110: image ideal and finite chart generators; extension to fine log schemes by the same image-ideal construction.

proof.text: Write $J\subseteq\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$ for the sheaf ideal generated by $\alpha(\mathcal I)$. Choose a covering by affine coherent charts $u:U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to X$ with finite generators $E\subset P$. On the slice over $U$, every section of $\mathcal I$ is locally $e m$ for some $e\in E$ and $m\in M$. Consequently $\alpha(e m)=\alpha(e)\alpha(m)$ belongs to the ideal generated by the $\alpha(e)$; the reverse inclusion holds because $E\subset\mathcal I$. Thus $J|_U$ is the image sheaf of $\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}^{\oplus E}\to\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$, $(b_e)\mapsto\sum_e b_e\alpha(e)$. The argument uses local membership, not an assertion that all sections of a sheaf image lift globally.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.3.7, printed p. 107; 3.4.2, printed p. 110 (image-ideal construction).

proof.text: On such a chart define $L_U$ as the Zariski sheaf image of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus E}\to\mathcal O_U$ with the same formula. The source and target are quasi-coherent: on each affine open they are the tilde modules of a finite free module and the ring. The quasi-coherent image theorem gives that $L_U$ is quasi-coherent and $\Gamma(U,L_U)=(\alpha(e):e\in E)=:I_E\subset A$. The affine tilde counit therefore identifies $L_U\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_U$ with $\widetilde{I_E}\hookrightarrow\widetilde A$, including the map, by its naturality. Etale association is the tensor pullback $\epsilon_U^*$ (written $L_U$ in that node), a left adjoint preserving all colimits with $\epsilon_U^*\mathcal O_U\simeq\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$ [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom]; it therefore preserves the finite direct sum and the epimorphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus E}\twoheadrightarrow L_U$. Exactness of etale association, applied to $0\to L_U\to\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal O_U/L_U\to0$ (all three quasi-coherent by the image theorem), keeps $(L_U)_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}$ a monomorphism. Hence $(L_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the image of the associated free-module map, which by step 1 is $J|_U$. The identification sends every local section to the same section of the structure sheaf.

Each $(L_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ is site quasi-coherent by the etale equivalence. The predicate is local, so the chart identifications of step 2 show that $J$ is site quasi-coherent on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$: for an arbitrary object, pull back the chart cover and then the local free presentations. Apply the equivalence on $X$ to obtain a quasi-coherent Zariski module $K$ with $K_{\mathrm{et}}=J$. Use its inverse, restriction to Zariski opens, on the inclusion $J\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}$. The open-section identity makes $K(W)=J(W)\subseteq\mathcal O_X(W)$ for every Zariski open $W$, so this is an ideal subsheaf, not only an abstract isomorphism class. The same inverse shows uniqueness as an ideal with its inclusion. Locally on the etale site, step 1 is an epimorphism from a finite free module to $J$; the finite-type comparison therefore makes $K$ of finite type. This does not assert coherence of $K$ on a non-Noetherian scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem logIdeal_image_exists_unique {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : EtaleLogStructure X)
    (hM : M.IsFine) (I : M.IdealFamily) (hI : M.IsNonemptyFineCoherentIdeal I) :
    ∃ K : X.IdealSheafData,
      Scheme.Modules.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType K.toModules ∧
      M.IsImageIdealAlgebraization I K ∧
      ∀ L : X.IdealSheafData, M.IsImageIdealAlgebraization I L → L = K
